title: Customer status templates and ops cheatfile
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical cheatfile for incident communications — focused on status page wording, customer-facing notes, quick Slack broadcasts, and the essential war-room checklist. Intended to be used by on-call responders and comms leads when an event requires public updates. Draft notes and TODOs are sprinkled in; this is intentionally lightweight so it can be edited in-the-moment.

Key principles (short):
- Clarity over cleverness: plain language, expected impact, and next steps.
- Timeboxed cadence: set expectation for update frequency up-front.
- Single source of truth: link the incident ticket and the public status page in every update.
- Respect privacy: don’t promise root cause until confirmed; avoid PII.

Incident severity -> comms posture (quick map):
- Sev1 (major outage, partial or full service disruption): open public status page, send initial customer note within 15–30 minutes, update every 30 min until stabilized.
- Sev2 (degraded performance or significant feature outage): status page + targeted customer notes within 60 minutes, updates every 60 min.
- Sev3 (minor impact, intermittent errors): internal alert first, public status page only if customer-visible and persists >2 hours.

Status page templates (replace placeholders: {incident_id}, {service}, {region}, {eta}, {mitigation}):
1) Initial (short):
Title: {service} degraded — investigating
Body: We are investigating reports of degraded performance for {service} impacting some customers in {region}. Our team is actively investigating. Incident: {incident_id}. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Link to incident: {ticket_url}
Severity: Investigating

2) Investigating (middle update):
Title: {service} outage — updates ongoing
Body: We have identified an elevated error rate affecting {service} for customers in {region}. Engineers are collecting diagnostics and running mitigations. No ETA yet. We will update by {next_update_time}. Incident: {incident_id}.

3) Mitigating (when workaround applied):
Title: Mitigation in progress for {service}
Body: We have applied a mitigative change that has reduced error rates for {service}. Some customers may still see intermittent issues while we validate full recovery. Current ETA for full recovery: {eta}. Continued monitoring in progress. Incident: {incident_id}.

4) Monitoring (post-mitigate):
Title: {service} performance improving; monitoring
Body: Metrics show steady improvement and error rates are returning to normal for {service}. Our team will continue monitoring for the next {monitor_window}. If you are still seeing problems, please reach out to support. Incident: {incident_id}.

5) Resolved (final):
Title: Incident resolved — {service}
Body: The incident affecting {service} in {region} has been resolved. Root cause analysis is in progress and will be shared in the postmortem. If you continue to experience issues, contact support with the incident ID {incident_id}.

Customer email templates (short, targeted):
- Initial (to affected customers):
Subject: Incident {incident_id}: {service} degraded
Hi — we’re investigating an issue affecting {service} that may impact your workflows. Our engineers are working on a fix. We’ll update you within {update_window}. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or open a ticket. — The Redwood Inference SRE team

- Follow-up (after mitigation):
Subject: Update on {incident_id}: progress on {service}
Hi — we rolled a mitigation that reduced the impact for most customers. Our team is validating. We expect full recovery by {eta}. We’ll follow up when the incident is fully resolved.

- Post-resolution (post-incident summary brief):
Subject: {incident_id} resolved — summary and next steps
Hi — Incident {incident_id} affecting {service} has been resolved. We are preparing a postmortem with timeline, root cause, and remediation actions. Estimated delivery: {pm_deadline}. Thank you for your patience.

Internal war-room checklist (one-pager):
- Triage & scope (first 10 mins):
  - Confirm the on-call has ownership; create/confirm incident ticket (e.g., SRE-2029).
  - Short description, severity, impacted customers/regions, initial metrics.
  - Assign roles: incident lead, comms lead, mitigation owner, list of SMEs.
- Communications (first 15 mins):
  - Post initial status page message (use template).
  - Post Slack alert to #sre-oncall and #ops-updates with incident link.
  - Notify customer success for high-value customers (include account names if known).
- Investigation & mitigation (ongoing):
  - Capture key timestamps in ticket: detection, mitigation start, mitigation end.
  - Temporary mitigations: feature flags, traffic routing, rollback.
  - If escalating to infra team or hardware vendor, log contacts and ticket numbers.
- Update cadence & handoffs:
  - Set explicit next update time and stick to it. Typical cadence: 30m for Sev1, 60m for Sev2.
  - Handoffs: on-call to follow-up engineer must include a 5-min debrief and ticket updates.
- Customer follow-through & closure:
  - Send final status page update and customer email.
  - Create a postmortem ticket and assign owner.
  - Add communication timeline to postmortem (copy status page updates).

Quick Slack broadcast templates (short & copyable):
- Initial: :rotating_light: Incident {incident_id} — {service} degraded in {region}. Investigating. Ticket: {ticket_url}
- Mitigated: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied for {incident_id}. Performance improving; monitoring.
- Resolved: :tada: {incident_id} resolved. Root cause analysis underway.

Escalation decision points (cheats):
- No mitigation or regression after 2 mitigation attempts -> escalate to infra lead and exec oncall.
- >10% of customer requests failed for >15 minutes -> notify CS leadership and prepare customer emails.
- Data integrity concerns -> immediate pause of affected subsystems and exec escalation.

Post-incident comms owner checklist (before closing incident):
- Ensure status page final update posted.
- Customer emails sent to affected lists.
- Support tickets for impacted customers are triaged and follow-ups assigned.
- Postmortem ticket created with comms timeline and draft executive summary.

Notes to self / things to consider for later iterations:
- Create short canned templates for enterprise customers (include SLA statements and support contacts).
- Automate status page update creation from incident ticket (reduce manual typos).
- Provide a quick link set in the on-call doc: dashboards, log queries, runbooks for DBs, cache, networking.

Useful links (placeholders to replace in live doc):
- Incident ticket: {ticket_url}
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.example/edit
- Monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/sre-overview

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who is the canonical comms approver for Sev1 external emails? (ops vs. customer success?)
- Add a short template for multi-region partial outage with per-region ETA fields.
- Decide whether internal broadcast should include estimated customer impact percentages by default.

Version notes:
- v0.1 initial draft (this doc) — compact, low-friction templates.
- v0.2: add enterprise templates and automation notes.

---
If you’re the on-call: copy a template above into status.redwood, paste incident link into Slack, and ping the comms lead. Keep updates punctual.

End of cheatfile.
